messages:
maria: Customer says they started getting intermittent 429s on POST /v1/generate after flipping traffic through our service mesh. Happens ~1-2x/min for project proj-abc, other projects unaffected. Customer attached request id list and says it started after proxy config change.

devin: can you paste one of the request ids and a sample request/headers? also which auth method are they using (API key vs org token)?

maria: here's one id: req-20240318-xyz. Customer says they use an API key in X-API-Key header; mesh team says they add an Authorization: Bearer <token> for internal tracing. They included this minimal curl:

```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-prod-abc123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer internal-service-token" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","input":"hello"}'\n```

rate_limiter_bot: 429 | scope=project:proj-abc | reason=quota_exhausted | window=60s | quota=120rpm | usage=121 | ip=34.120.5.12

sre_clara: quick hypothesis: if the mesh strips or rewrites headers, our auth lookup might miss the X-API-Key and fall back to IP-based attribution (nat IP -> project mapping). If the project quota is lower than org quota, that would explain 429s only for that project. Also risk if both headers present and we recently changed precedence logic.

eng_aaron: we rolled a tiny change last week that altered auth precedence when both Authorization and X-API-Key are supplied by a proxied request. We intended to prefer X-API-Key first, but codepath might pick Authorization in some fast-paths. Will check commit diff.

devin: can we confirm whether requests that 429 include X-API-Key in raw incoming headers? maria, do we have the raw edge logs showing header presence?

maria: attached snippet from edge logs (redacted):

```\nIN: req-20240318-xyz src=10.4.2.11 NAT=34.120.5.12 headers={"content-type":"application/json","authorization":"Bearer internal-service-token"}\n```

note: X-API-Key missing in that capture.

sre_clara: that looks like the mesh removed X-API-Key before sending to us. When that happens, attribution falls back to NAT IP mapping which is mapped to proj-abc and that project is hitting its RPM quota. Mesh team probably strips sensitive headers by default.

eng_aaron: okay, root cause looks like header stripping + our precedence change. Short-term mitigations:
- ask customer/mesh to whitelist X-API-Key (or pass it as Authorization Bearer token we recognise)
- temporarily raise proj-abc project quota
- patch runtime to prefer API key if present earlier in request pipeline (I'll open a PR)

devin: repro plan for SRE: 1) emulate mesh by sending request from our test-nat egress without X-API-Key but with Authorization header, 2) send same from egress with X-API-Key present, 3) compare attribution & limiter events.

maria: I'll reply to customer: explain mesh likely strips their header, ask them to either preserve X-API-Key or use a single Authorization header we can accept, and offer a temporary quota bump while they fix mesh. Will also include our repro steps and ask for permission to test from their environment.

eng_aaron: opened internal ticket INC-2024-789 and assigned to eng-runtime. I'll attach commit diff and put a short hotfix branch if we need immediate behavior revert.

sre_clara: I'll run the repro from test-nat now and post results.

sre_clara: repro done — confirmed: requests without X-API-Key are attributed to project via NAT IP; requests with X-API-Key get API-key-based attribution and avoid project quota. Adding X-API-Key in Authorization: Bearer <key> also works (we map bearer token to api-key when configured).

maria: thanks everyone — sending customer message now and will follow up after eng-runtime updates. Keeping thread open until hotfix or customer fix is verified. :thumbsup:
